prompt:

Conforming purchase loans, manual underwriting: eligibility rules (2026)

R2. A short sale must be at least 4 years old, or at least 2 years old with documented extenuating circumstances.
R3. The debt-to-income ratio may not exceed 36%, unless the credit score is at least 720, reserves cover at least 6 months, and the ratio is at most 45%.
R4. At least 7 years must have passed since a foreclosure was completed.
R5. Monthly debts including the new housing payment may not exceed 45% of stable gross monthly income.
R6. At least 4 years must have passed since a Chapter 7 bankruptcy was discharged. This rule does not apply if extenuating circumstances are documented and at least 2 years have passed.
R7. When the loan-to-value ratio is above 75%, the credit score must be at least 680.
R8. If the credit history section is silent, assume no bankruptcy, foreclosure or short sale.
R9. The representative credit score must be at least 660.
R10. The loan-to-value ratio (loan amount over property value) may not exceed 90%.

Funds totaling $40,000 are being provided by a family member to assist with the transaction. Documentation confirming the transfer of gift funds has not been submitted by the donor. Verification shows the applicant has accumulated 3 years of experience in the current profession. The applicant notes in personal statements a history of consistent, on-time payments across all financial commitments. The bureau data establishes a representative credit score of 600. No formal documentation regarding unusual or uncontrollable past hardships has been provided. All individuals listed on the mortgage will reside in the property as their primary residence. The total debt-to-income ratio, inclusive of the proposed housing expense, calculates to 18%. Having had no ownership interest in residential real estate over the preceding three years, the applicant meets first-time homebuyer criteria. Remaining liquid funds are sufficient to cover 23 months of total housing payments following the transaction. Completion of specialized education or training for the current line of work occurred under a year ago. The established value for the property is $1,400,000, representing the lesser of the purchase price and the appraised value. Verified balances across checking, savings, and eligible retirement accounts amount to $45,000. The loan-to-value ratio is calculated at 21%. The total funds required from the borrower at settlement equal $35,000. Recurring obligations, including credit cards, auto loans, and installment accounts, total $150 per month. The subject property is located in a county subject to standard baseline loan limits. The credit history shows a Chapter 7 bankruptcy discharged 5 years ago. The applicant is raising two children independently. Income verification documents substantiate a gross monthly income of $12,000. The applicant relocated to the United States from another country eleven years ago. The projected monthly housing expense, including principal, interest, taxes, insurance, and any applicable assessments, is $2,100.

Conforming purchase loans, manual underwriting: eligibility rules (2026)
A loan application is approved only if it meets every rule below. Ratios are whole percentages rounded down. Rules marked as defaults say what to assume when the file is silent on a point.

R1. The debt-to-income ratio may not exceed 36%, unless the credit score is at least 700, reserves cover at least 6 months, and the ratio is at most 45%.
R2. If a co-borrower will not live in the home, the loan-to-value ratio may not exceed 90%.
R3. Monthly debts including the new housing payment may not exceed 45% of stable gross monthly income.
R4. The loan-to-value ratio (loan amount over property value) may not exceed 90%.
R5. When the loan-to-value ratio is above 75%, the credit score must be at least 680.
R6. The loan amount may not exceed the conforming limit of $832,750.
R7. The representative credit score must be at least 640.
R8. If the credit history section is silent, assume no bankruptcy, foreclosure or short sale.
R9. At least 4 years must have passed since a Chapter 7 bankruptcy was discharged. This rule does not apply if extenuating circumstances are documented and at least 2 years have passed.
R10. If the file does not mention a co-borrower living elsewhere, assume every borrower will live in the home.
R11. At least 7 years must have passed since a foreclosure was completed. This rule does not apply if extenuating circumstances are documented, at least 3 years have passed, and the loan-to-value ratio is at most 90%.

The credit history shows a Chapter 7 bankruptcy discharged 3 years ago. Eligible liquid assets held solely by the borrower total $130,000. The subject property is located in a county that falls under the baseline loan limit. Ownership history records show the borrower is not a first-time home buyer. Factoring in the proposed housing expense, the total debt-to-income ratio is 22%. The applicant has not participated in any formal schooling or training programs recently. The requested mortgage amount is $540,000. Submitted paperwork establishes that the past credit impairment stemmed from an unexpected involuntary termination. Employment verification confirms the borrower has maintained continuous employment in the same industry for 10 years. A parent who will reside elsewhere is joined on the loan application as a non-occupant co-borrower. The established value of the real estate is $1,050,000, representing the lesser of the purchase price and the appraised value.
